title: 2007 AMC 8 Problem 16
statement: Amanda Reckonwith draws five circles with radii \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4\) and \(5.\) Then for each circle she plots the point \((C, A),\) where \(C\) is its circumference and \(A\) is its area. Which of the following could be her graph?

solutions.text:
The circumferences of circles with radii \(1\) through \(5\) are \(2\pi,\) \(4\pi,\) \(6\pi,\) \(8\pi,\) and \(10\pi\). Their respective areas are \(\pi,\) \(4\pi,\) \(9\pi,\) \(16\pi,\) and \(25\pi\).

As \(C\) increases by equal amounts, \(A\) increases more and more quickly, so the points form an increasing quadratic pattern. Only graph A has that shape.

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Write circumference and area in terms of the radius.
As the circumference grows linearly with radius, the area grows quadratically.
